harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-member MariaDB 10.5 Galera cluster on node1-node3 (AlmaLinux 9, mariadb-server + mariadb-server-galera + galera from appstream), bootstrapped on node1 with sample appdb.items data, and joined node2/node3 via mariabackup SST (required opening firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444 and a custom SELinux module to permit the mariadb-backup connectto AVC that was blocking SST). Added node4 as a fourth member: installed the same packages, configured galera.cnf with wsrep_cluster_address including node4, and it joined via SST carrying the full existing dataset (cluster_size 4, Synced/Primary) and was confirmed to accept writes that replicated to the other members. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured a boot_id + cluster-health baseline on all 4 nodes, then rebooted them one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirming a changed boot_id and full quorum/Synced/Primary recovery (with pre-existing data intact) before moving to the next node. A final write on node1 after all restarts replicated correctly to node4.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes and confirmed MariaDB/Galera was not preinstalled; found AlmaLinux 9 appstream packages mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera on node1, node2, node3, node4
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on all 4 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all 4 nodes
Generated sstuser and root passwords on node1 via openssl rand, distributed via secret_env only
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-node3 with wsrep_cluster_address gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and wsrep_sst_method=mariabackup
Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, created sstuser grant, set root password, created appdb.items with sample rows
Diagnosed and fixed a mariadb-backup SELinux AVC denial (connectto on mysqld_t unix socket) blocking SST by compiling and loading a minimal local policy module on all 4 nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to the cluster via mariabackup SST after clearing their datadirs; verified cluster_size 2 then 3 with full data replication
Verified multi-master writes: insert on node3 visible on node1
Reconfigured wsrep_cluster_address to include node4 on node1-node3 (no restart needed, address list only used at connect time)
Configured galera.cnf on node4 and started mariadb; node4 joined via SST as the 4th member with full existing dataset (cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary)
Verified node4 accepts writes that replicate to node2
Enabled mariadb service on boot on all 4 nodes; propagated root credentials via /root/.my.cnf on all nodes
Captured boot_id and Galera health baseline (cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary) on all 4 nodes

Rebooted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling until exec available, confirming changed boot_id and full cluster recovery (quorum, Synced, Primary, intact data) before proceeding to the next node
Performed a final post-restart write on node1 and confirmed replication to node4

evidence.requirement: 3-member Galera cluster running on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped with sample appdb.items data; node2 and node3 joined via SST reaching cluster_size 3, Synced; write from node3 replicated to node1 proving multi-master write capability across the 3-member cluster.

evidence.requirement: node4 added as 4th member carrying existing data
evidence.summary: After starting mariadb on node4 with wsrep_cluster_address including node4, it joined via mariabackup SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size=4, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and SELECT on appdb.items shows all pre-existing rows (widget/gadget/gizmo/from-node3) present on node4.

evidence.requirement: node4 accepts writes like other members
evidence.summary: Insert executed directly on node4 (from-node4 row) and confirmed present via SELECT on node2, proving node4 participates as a full write-accepting member with wsrep_cluster_size=4 on node2.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 54bd1c3e captured with cluster healthy (size 4, Synced, Primary); systemctl reboot issued; node briefly unreachable; new boot_id 1db07335 confirmed changed; post-reboot check shows mariadb active, cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary, and appdb.items data intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e31962a9 captured with cluster healthy; systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable transiently; new boot_id 7de1ebd3 confirmed changed; after brief SST/IST catch-up, mariadb active with cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary, data intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31b01b46 captured with cluster healthy; systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable transiently; new boot_id 2ddfef71 confirmed changed; post-reboot check shows mariadb active, cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary, data intact.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4a743885 captured with cluster healthy; systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable transiently; new boot_id 78bb85f4 confirmed changed; post-reboot check shows mariadb active, cluster_size 4, Synced, Primary, data intact.

evidence.requirement: Full cluster remains functional and consistent after all 4 restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart-cycle write issued on node1 (post-restart-node1 row) and confirmed present in identical form when queried on node4, proving cross-node write/replication consistency after the full restart sequence.
